author: Felipe Blassioli
abstract: Decides WHERE work runs and on which tier + effort. Answers placement first — this session, a delegated subagent, or a fresh session — because placement is the larger lever: delegating keeps a unit's tokens out of the session prefix, and in measured local history turn count and context length dominate a session's cost while the tier is roughly a 2x multiplier on top. Then routes the tier by task characteristics from the routing_rubric in ~/.claude/model-profiles.md, applies consequence_override (reversibility outranks difficulty, in both directions), and resolves the target: a model string from tier_to_model for work that runs as a session, or the Agent-tool model alias from delegation_aliases for delegated work — different value spaces, and an unset alias makes a subagent inherit the caller's model. Handles the mid-run question too: reads execution_signals to say whether to escalate, de-escalate, compact, hand off, or restart, and requires externalizing durable state before any of the last three. Names the signal that would flip its own verdict. Holds no inline routing data — the shared file is read at runtime, so nothing rots on a model release; emits tier + effort even when the model table is unreadable, and flags only the profile half that actually aged out. The same file is read by prompt-audit, tailor-to-fable, and the loop-compiler plugin.
